riley_hillside: A bare grassy slope above a Derbyshire farm in August 1666, thin turf over grey limestone, the Peak District moors rolling away to the horizon under a hard pale summer sky. A lone figure — a farmer's wife in plain 17th-century woollen dress and apron, dark skirt, linen cap — always seen from behind, in silhouette, from a distance, or with her face turned away and never resolved; a spade, freshly turned earth, a low mound. Dignified, desolate, sunlit but cheerless. 1666 photoreal cinematic, NOT modern farmland, no fences, no modern walls, no telegraph poles.
riley_farmhouse: A small poor 17th-century Derbyshire hill farm of rough grey stone with a low thatched or stone-slab roof, tiny windows, a heavy plank door, set apart and alone on the edge of moorland. Interior: a single dim room, earth or stone-flagged floor, a cold hearth, a wooden trestle, plain pewter and wood, low smoke-darkened beams. Figures only ever from behind or in deep shadow, faces never resolved. Overcast grey light through small panes. 1666 photoreal cinematic, period-accurate, no modern objects.
eyam_village: A small 17th-century English Peak District village of grey limestone cottages with thatched and stone-slab roofs lining a narrow lane, a low Saxon church tower, dry-stone walls, kitchen gardens. Deserted, shuttered, doors marked, no crowds — emptiness and stillness carry the dread. Any figures distant, from behind, silhouetted, faces never resolved. Overcast, muted, mournful palette. 1666 photoreal cinematic, the medieval village NOT a modern restored tourist village, no tarmac, no modern signage.
boundary_stone: A weathered grey gritstone boundary marker at the edge of the village where the moorland begins, with several round holes bored into its top. Coins sit in the holes, submerged in vinegar; a basket of provisions left on the grass beside it. No people at the stone, or a single distant figure walking away. Cold overcast Derbyshire light, wet grass, the empty moor beyond. 1666 photoreal cinematic, no modern path, no modern objects.
village_church: The exterior and churchyard of a small ancient Derbyshire parish church, squat Saxon stone tower, weathered standing cross, leaning gravestones, a low stone wall, yew trees. Fresh-dug graves, bare earth. A single fresh grave near the cross for the closing of Catherine's strand. Overcast, still, solemn. 1666 photoreal cinematic, the original 17th-century church, NOT a modern restored churchyard, no modern headstones, no modern paths.
riley_graves_closing: Seven simple weathered stone grave markers on an open grassy hillside, ringed by a single low dry-stone wall, entirely alone in a wide empty field with the Derbyshire moors stretching to the horizon and no village anywhere in sight. Long grass moving in the wind, pale overcast sky, utterly silent and solitary. The closing image of the film. 1666 period graves seen as they stand weathered and old, photoreal cinematic, no modern fences, no modern monuments, no visitors, no signage.
